rotation_phase.label: Late Cycle
rotation_phase.reasoning: Energy and Basic Materials are leading year-to-date performance while defensive sectors like Utilities and Healthcare are lagging, which is highly characteristic of a classic Late Cycle phase.

watchlist.name: Technology
watchlist.thesis: Strongest absolute momentum score of 0.729 paired with the second-highest YTD rank confirms powerful, sustained market leadership.

watchlist.name: Energy
watchlist.thesis: Holding the number one YTD rank alongside an elite momentum score of 0.714 signals persistent, top-tier structural strength.

watchlist.name: Industrials
watchlist.thesis: A high momentum score of 0.714 matching Energy confirms robust, broad-based cyclical demand as it maintains its top-three YTD position.

sectors.note:
Defensive and lagging sectors are rapidly gaining momentum as investors seek safety. Healthcare is leading this rotation, climbing 3.3% over the past month with a rising momentum score of 0.600, despite its negative year-to-date performance. Consumer Defensive and Real Estate are also attracting capital, posting the strongest weekly gains at 4.0% and 1.0% respectively.

In contrast, high-flying growth and cyclical sectors are sharply losing ground. Technology experienced a severe weekly pullback of 8.3%, while Basic Materials and Communication Services plunged 9.3% and 7.5% over the past month. Consumer Cyclical remains the weakest performer overall, extending its year-to-date decline to 6.9% after another negative week.

A notable divergence is occurring between long-term trend leaders and short-term performance. While Technology and Energy still command the highest overall momentum scores and lead YTD gains, their recent weekly declines suggest a tactical pause. Investors should watch whether this defensive rotation into Healthcare and Real Estate represents a temporary hedging maneuver or a structural shift away from growth.

industries.note:
Capital is rotating into defensive staples, niche logistics, and select beaten-down value plays. Trucking continues to show exceptional strength, up 22.2% over the month. Meanwhile, Food Distribution and Medical Distribution are gaining sharp weekly momentum, joined by consumer staples like non-alcoholic beverages and household products, signaling a sudden flight to safer, cash-flowing sectors.

Conversely, commodities and clean energy are losing substantial ground. Gold, Silver, and Uranium are in freefall, each posting double-digit weekly losses and deep monthly declines. This liquidation extends to previous industrial leaders like Electrical Equipment & Parts, which fell 12.0% this week, and Solar, which collapsed 20.2%, indicating aggressive profit-taking. 

A stark divergence is unfolding in technology. High-flying hardware segments like Semiconductor Equipment and Computer Hardware remain long-term leaders despite recent weekly pullbacks. However, Software (both Application and Infrastructure) is deeply negative on the year, confirming that investors are favoring physical computing infrastructure over software platforms in this current cycle.
